text:
dave.customer: Hi — hitting intermittent timeouts when streaming from /v1/chat/completions. Client sees a few SSE chunks then the connection closes after ~8s. Request ID I can see in our client logs: rwx-789. Using our prod token behind a corporate proxy. Example curl I tried:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test long"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```
Anyone seen this pattern?

alice.support: Sorry about that — thanks for the details. Can you paste the full `-v` output (headers) and confirm the exact X-Request-Id from our response headers if present? Also quick repro step: try forcing HTTP/1.1 + no buffering and see if it changes behavior: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test long"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```
Please also tell us region (us-west-2 / eu-west-1 etc.) and whether you have a proxy that might be buffering.

dave.customer: Pasted the verbose output below. We do see `:status: 200` and `x-request-id: rwx-789` in the headers, then a few `data:` SSE lines and then `* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact` with no more data. Region is us-west-2. We do have a corporate proxy (explicit HTTP proxy) that does TLS intercept. Token was rotated yesterday but the same key repros. Full snippet (redacted keys):

```
> POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/2
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Content-Type: application/json
> Accept: text/event-stream
< HTTP/2 200
< date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:12 GMT
< x-request-id: rwx-789
< content-type: text/event-stream
data: {"id":"ch_01","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[...]}

data: {"choices": [...]}

* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```

carol.engineering: Thanks — I pulled rwx-789 from our logs. We had a short spike of HTTP/2 stream resets in us-west-2 around that time (15:02 UTC). There is a known path where some corporate proxies that do TLS MITM + HTTP/2 downgrade can send unexpected GOAWAY/RST_STREAM frames when they see long-lived chunked responses. For a quick validation, forcing HTTP/1.1 usually avoids the issue. Can you also try adding `Connection: keep-alive` and `Accept: text/event-stream` (SSE) headers when reproducing?

alice.support: If the HTTP/1.1 repro shows stable streaming, we'll escalate to infra to add an automatic HTTP/2 fallback policy for proxied clients. Please run the following and paste the entire output (so we can attach it to the debug bundle):
```
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test long"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -o /tmp/stream.out
```
Also upload `/tmp/stream.out` plus the `-v` logs to the support portal and mention rwx-789 so we can link it.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-045 to track HTTP/2 stream resets in us-west-2.

dave.customer: Ran the forced HTTP/1.1 command. Good news — streaming stayed open and we received the full event set. No premature connection close. I uploaded `/tmp/stream.out` and the `curl -v` output to the portal, linked rwx-789.

alice.support: Great — thanks for validating and for the debug bundle. I'll escalate to infra (CC'ing eng). For short-term mitigation, use the `--http1.1` flag or set your upstream proxy to not force HTTP/2 for this host. We'll track a permanent fix in INC-2026-045 and post updates here. ETA: infra will triage today and aim for a patch/route rule within 48–72 hours.

dave.customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick help. Will keep using the HTTP/1.1 workaround. :thumbsup:

carol.engineering: Noted. We'll also add a test to our synthetic suite to detect this class of resets behind proxies. If anything changes I'll update the incident.

alice.support: Closing loop after infra patch — will post incident update and recommended client config. If you see any other request ids, please drop them here. Thanks!
